branches.name: bloodline
branches.why: NOT A SWARM DECK. The 400-game Forge run killed that thesis: composite won 31/400 against the champion's 50/400, interval on the difference excluding zero, and the mechanism was one number -- combat damage dealt to players fell 29.07 to 18.20 because 1/1 tokens do not connect against real blockers. So the tokens stop being the clock and become FUEL. OUT go the arrival-damage payoffs that pay 1-2 per 1/1 (Impact Tremors, Witty Roastmaster, Warleader's Call, Corpse Knight, Mirkwood Bats, Purphoros) and the go-wide combat payoffs. IN come free sacrifice outlets (Viscera Seer, Ashnod's Altar, Altar of Dementia), the dig they feed (Liliana Dreadhorde General draws on every creature death; Bloodtracker; High-Society Hunter), and the payoffs that eat tokens and get big: Yahenni and Immersturm Predator turn a token into INDESTRUCTIBLE, Vish Kal turns one into +X/+X and then into removal, Bloodflow Connoisseur is the cheap version. Crossway Troublemakers gives every attacking Vampire deathtouch AND lifelink, which is what makes a board of any size unprofitable to block. Altar of Dementia mills OPPONENTS, which grows The Haunt of Hightower and the Nighthawk Scavenger already in the 99 -- self-mill would bury the payoffs, opponent-mill feeds them. THE GOLDFISH IS NOT THE ARBITER HERE and is expected to under-rate this: it has no blockers, so it rewards exactly the wide board the real table just ate. Forge decides.
branches.state_why: merged 2026-09-01 into the list after VNone

proposal.why: The only one of six branches that beats the checked-in list on anything at a real table. 400 Forge games per arm against the pilot's own pod at one seed: +6.91 combat damage [0.07, 13.76] and +0.46 casts [0.01, 0.92], both excluding zero. It pays 1.17 drain for that, which is also real and six times smaller. Win rate 0.142 against 0.125 is NOT resolvable and is not claimed. Selected over composite, drain-engine, mana-recovery and two bloodline revisions after every arm was re-derived under the corrected metrics.

branches.name: bloodline-v2
branches.why: Sharpening bloodline, which is the first list this session to beat the champion at a real table: 57/400 against 50/400, and combat damage 35.98 against 29.07 -- the exact number the swarm build collapsed on. Six swaps from two independent sources agreeing with the Forge evidence. H1 REMOVE THE BLOCKERS RATHER THAN OUT-SIZE THEM: Grave Pact makes every token death an edict on the whole table, which deletes the blockers that made 1/1s worthless instead of trying to punch through them. H2 Yawgmoth, Thran Physician is a free sacrifice outlet AND removal AND the dig, in one card the pilot already owns. H3 Necropotence, also owned, because the modelled draw is four cards and the rest is sacrifice-gated. H4 Swords to Plowshares is the format's #11 card and sits in 67% of Edgar decks; this one ran none. Phyrexian Altar over a colourless outlet because mana-analysis has flagged the colour gap on every version. Priest of Forgotten Gods is drain, edict, draw and ramp on one two-mana body. Cuts are by format consensus: Vish Kal at #15903 was my pick and seven mana, and the field disagrees hard.
branches.state_why: no proposal — this is an experiment, not a decision

branches.name: bloodline-v3
branches.why: Built from BLOODLINE, not from v2, because v2 was killed at 208 games on a pre-committed criterion: combat damage mean 31.38 against bloodline's 35.98 and a win rate of 0.115 against 0.142. The diagnosis is arithmetic I should have caught before spending the run -- v2 traded FIVE CREATURES for FOUR SPELLS, and fewer attackers is less damage. That is the same error mana-recovery made when it bought interaction with three bodies. So every addition here is a CREATURE, and all six come out of yawgmoth-swarm, which the pilot has agreed to break down. Grave Titan is a 6/6 deathtouch that makes four power of 2/2 tokens on entry AND on every attack -- a giant that brings its own fuel, and 2/2s are not the 1/1s the pod blocked all day. Mikaeus gives every non-Human +1/+1 and UNDYING, so the giants come back bigger from the wipes the captain's log keeps losing to. Carrion Feeder does Bloodflow Connoisseur's job for two mana less. Ophiomancer mints a free deathtouch blocker every upkeep. Ayara drains on every BLACK creature entering, and eminence tokens are black Vampires, so every Vampire cast now drains twice. Marauding Blight-Priest turns this deck's heavy lifelink into reach.

branches.name: bloodline-v4
branches.why: A SEPARATE BRANCH, not a stage onto bloodline: bloodline is PROPOSED as v1.0.1 and staging would make that proposal stale and un-freeze a decision already accepted. Aimed at the one measured cost bloodline pays -- stall 5 games in 100 to 8 -- WITHOUT touching the gains it bought. The diagnosis says this is a curve problem and not a mana problem: supply is identical to v1.0.0 (mana at turn five 4.944 against 4.936, missed land drops 0.404 both), and mana_short rose 40% purely because bloodline swapped two- and three-drops for six-drops. So attack it from both ends. CURVE DOWN seven mana: Vish Kal at seven is the card the field ranks #15903 and that two earlier revisions both cut; Bloodtracker pays life for counters a sac deck gets free; Unbounded Potential is a pump spell. ACCELERATION IN: Culling the Weak sacrifices a token for BBBB, so it is ramp that eats fuel the deck already makes and turns turn three into a six-drop turn -- the pilot's stated T4/T5 pump. THE COUNTER ENGINE: The Ozolith banks counters off every creature that LEAVES the battlefield, which in a deck built on sacrifice means every eaten body reloads onto the next giant, for one mana. Aetherborn Marauder is the body that collects them, with flying and lifelink. Vault of the Archangel gives the whole team deathtouch and lifelink from a LAND slot rather than a spell slot, and it costs only a white source in a deck already at its white target while black and red are the short colours. NO COUNTER DOUBLER EXISTS IN THIS IDENTITY -- Ozolith, the Shattered Spire is green -- so that lever is unavailable and is not being chased.
branches.state_why: no proposal — this is an experiment, not a decision

branches.name: bloodline-v5
branches.why: HELD, NOT MEASURED. Opened so the hypothesis survives the session; no Forge run has been made and no figure here is evidence. Found by walking the Atlas synergy graph out from this deck's engine cards, where the heaviest edges were Counters + Tokens and Sac + Death Trigger. THE THESIS: counters are the fastest route to a big vampire in these colours, because +1/+1 counter DOUBLERS do not exist in BRW -- Ozolith, the Shattered Spire is green -- and PROLIFERATE is the colour-shifted substitute. Blade of the Bloodchief is the find and the pilot already owns it: one mana, equip one, and every creature death puts TWO counters on an equipped Vampire, which in a deck built on eating its own tokens is the fastest accelerant available. Dusk Legion Duelist converts that engine into cards, drawing whenever counters land on it, once a turn. Metastatic Evangel proliferates on every nontoken creature entering, and this deck casts about nine spells a game. ALL THREE COST ONE OR TWO MANA, which is deliberate: bloodline's only measured cost is stall rising from 5 games in 100 to 8, diagnosed as a CURVE problem against flat mana, and v4 failed trying to fix it with acceleration Forge would not cast. Cutting Vish Kal at seven, Bloodtracker at four and Unbounded Potential at two takes eight mana out of the curve while adding the counter engine. MILL WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: 89 BRW cards read an opponent's graveyard but this deck has only two payoffs and one enabler, self-mill buries the giants it is digging for, and going all-in on Altar of Dementia as a wincon is a different deck rather than an increment.
branches.state_why: no proposal — this is an experiment, not a decision

branches.name: composite
branches.why: Third hypothesis, and the one aimed at the frontier rather than at one axis. mana-recovery bought interaction affordability with THREE BODIES, and lost 1.53 damage at T10 for it. This buys the same mana by cutting NON-BODIES instead: Olivia's Wrath is a five-mana sweeper in a deck whose whole plan is a wide token board and it kills your own 1/1s; Pact of the Serpent is X-based draw the model cannot price and the table rarely casts; Timothar is the one body, and it measured neutral on every axis swept. If the mana was the lever and the bodies were the price, this should hold the damage and keep the interaction.

branches.name: drain-engine
branches.why: One axis, built deep: vampires enter -> tokens appear -> tokens convert into value -> drain closes. From captain's log 002 and the deck audit, which agree: card-advantage 4 v target 10, ramp 7 v 10-12, interaction 12 v target 5-6 and never castable. CUTS the anthem/+1+1/pump package and the Edgar attack plan (a six-drop whose payoff needs a board that survived, which this pod does not sell), plus 3 interaction slots the deck could never afford to hold up. ADDS the drain shell, sacrifice outlets and converters, and bodies that replace themselves. VAMPIRE-FIRST where the job is the same: eminence only mints a token when you cast a Vampire, so Scion of Opulence beats Pitiless Plunderer and Acolyte of Aclazotz beats a generic outlet. Ten of the seventeen adds are Vampires; seven came out of the Atlas library.

branches.name: mana-recovery
branches.why: HYPOTHESIS TEST off drain-engine, not a rival to it. Diagnosis: mana_short is 73% of the branch's stalls and mana at T5/T7 fell below v1.0.1 because the refactor cut Patchwork Banner, a rock, while deck-audit already had ramp UNDER target at 7 v 10-12. A one-for-one sweep moved stall by nothing on any of 11 candidates, because cheap cards cut mana_short and raise hand_empty and the two cancel. So the lever is compound: three mana sources for three off-axis spells. Deliberately does NOT cut Sanguine Bond (half a checker-verified infinite) or the X-based draw, which the model cannot price and would therefore recommend cutting for the wrong reason.

A token multiplier or extra token-maker drawn

A Vampire lord or anthem drawn (the combat plan)
THE SURVIVING INFINITE (stacks 004 and 006): Bloodthirsty Conqueror + a lifegain-loss half

engine.thesis: Edgar's eminence mints a free body every time you cast a Vampire and the doublers turn one mint into eight, so this deck wins by CASTING cheap creatures into a payoff that bills all three seats at once — and after the v1.0.0 baseline it does that by drawing more chances at the piece rather than by going and finding it.

diagnosis.verdict: It functions and every multi-card component turns over: 91.3% turn-3 land drop, a castable Vampire in 92.3% of games, lords 79.0%, a draw engine 73.3%. What I can measure end to end is conversion, and that is where it thins — THE GO-WIDE KILL assembles by turn six in 28.5% of games (mean turn 5.043), and its payoff leg is the thinnest of its three legs — six cards at 36.4% of openers against the multiplier's seven and the ignition leg's thirteen. That leg is now declared correctly: the group this document said was wrong in both directions has been split by trigger event, Mirkwood Bats is in it and the two death drains have a component of their own, and across 1,686 declare-attackers decisions in 180 games the pod attacks the biggest revealed damage dealer 69.5% of the time, ci95 [0.673, 0.717] against a uniform 50.6%, permutation p = 0.0001. Card draw is not what costs games: eleven real sources survive an oracle read against a floor of ten. Black may be — 30 sources of 36 and 82.2% on-curve with rocks against a cited 90% — and this document declines to rank it against conversion rather than pretending to, because the instrument that measures assembly cannot see colour at all; that ranking is routed, not decided here.

open_questions.question: Stack 011 settled the round-1 form of this: Mirkwood Bats triggers once per TOKEN, so N tokens created in one event is N triggers and N life per opponent, tracking the tokens and never the doublers. What 011 deliberately left counterfactual is the deck's own board — it holds ONE doubler and two opponents, and 010's eight-token board carries no Bats and ends with both opponents at 40. What does the real go-wide board put on the table: Bats plus two or three doublers into three untouched seats, and does Bloodletter of Aclazotz double it?

Does Bloodletter of Aclazotz double DAMAGE, not only stated life loss? Its reminder text reads '(Damage causes loss of life.)' and stack 004's checker treated the identical parenthetical on Bloodthirsty Conqueror as reminder text under 207.2a — but stacks 003 and 007 only ever tested 'each opponent loses N life' from Sanctum Seeker and Throne. Nobody has run the other direction: does Purphoros dealing 2 to each opponent become 4?

How many two-mana Vampire casts does the payoff suite need to take one seat from 40 to 0 with only ONE doubler on the battlefield? Stack 009 is exactly lethal at 12 life per seat and stack 008 measures 10 damage per cast with two doublers.

goldfish.py's _TUTOR_RE is the literal phrase 'search your library for a card' and deliberately excludes narrow tutors, so Forerunner of the Legion is not modelled — verified at source, and no longer the question. What is open: should it be, for a deck where 28 of the 99 are the searched type and the tutored card lands on top? And what does THE GO-WIDE KILL's assisted rate become if it is?

After this baseline the interactive suite covers 3 of 5 classes: deck-audit reads land and graveyard at zero, and reading all six removal spells confirms none answers a land. For a Mardu aggro deck whose pilot logged the whole table making him the archenemy on turn three, is a land answer or graveyard hate load-bearing, or is the correct trade exactly the one made — two premium white removal spells for more cheap Vampire bodies?

ANSWERED for its first half, still open for its second. The payoff group has been corrected and re-derived: the leg is six creation-and-entry payoffs at 36.4% of openers, 67.4% assembled, 56.7% by turn six; Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant hold their own component at 13.7% / 30.4% / 24.1%; and THE GO-WIDE KILL moved from 0.491 assembled and 0.327 by turn six to 0.445 and 0.285, mean turn 4.773 to 5.043. What remains unrun is the sandbox with this document's four (add, natural_cut) pairs applied, which is the only way to price two things it cannot derive: the payoff leg at eight copies against the kill's other two legs, and THE SURVIVING INFINITE once Sanguine Bond leaves its second group.

Mirkwood Bats reads 'whenever you create or sacrifice a token' where Caretaker's Talent reads 'whenever one or more tokens you control enter ... only once each turn'. When one eminence trigger creates eight tokens as a single replaced event (stack 010), does Mirkwood Bats trigger eight times or once?

Does Bloodletter of Aclazotz double DAMAGE as well as stated life loss? Stacks 003 and 007 only ever tested 'each opponent loses N life' from Sanctum Seeker and Throne of the God-Pharaoh; nobody has run Purphoros dealing 2 to each opponent through it.

What does the corpus say about typal and uncounterable mana against raw source counts? manabase.land_colors credits Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth and Cavern of Souls ZERO colour sources, so both left the 99 without moving the colour-sources axis by a single point, and no measured axis will move if either comes back.

Is the black shortfall costing this deck games, or is conversion? The bench cannot currently answer it: goldfish.py's `_mana_pips` reduces every cost to generic-equivalent mana and its mulligan rule counts lands rather than colours, so assembly rates, the turn-3 land drop and the keep rate are all colour-blind by construction, and mana_analysis's Karsten castability is a static hypergeometric that never meets the deck's curve. What would settle it is a colour-aware run: how often is a black spell in hand, affordable by total mana, and uncastable for want of a black source?

Does the death-drain line actually convert? It now has a measured rate — Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant, 30.4% assembled and 24.1% by turn six — and no checker-passed stack showing it closing a game. engine-critic established the deck can manufacture the death rather than wait for it (Skullclamp for {1} on a 1/1 token; Indulgent Aristocrat's outlet has no tap symbol and no timing restriction), so the question is how many deaths a seat costs at what mana, the way stack 009 did for the entry event.

"Two counters decided it" — Tom countered Champion of Dusk (the refuel the note calls "the refuel that would have closed the game") and Bloodthirsty Conqueror. With the wipes settled as variance and Edgar's timing settled as piloting, resolving a key spell through a seat holding counterspells is the one cause the note names that no artifact has looked at. Is that also variance, or is it a real property of a deck that is the table's archenemy from turn three?

piloting.reading: our seat was handled about as well as the pod, so an A/B between two of your own lists against this table is played equally badly on both sides and remains informative. It is still not a claim about how the deck plays in your hands.
